text: When Father Hooper at last lay dying, Elizabeth, whose calm affection had endured in secret through all those years, sat by his bed as his nurse. <break time="0.8s" /> The Reverend Mister Clark of Westbury, a young minister, bent forward and said, Before the veil of eternity is lifted, let me cast aside this black veil. <break time="0.8s" /> But Father Hooper snatched both his hands from beneath the bedclothes and pressed them strongly on the black veil, crying, Never, On earth, never. <break time="0.8s" /> Why do you tremble at me alone, he cried, turning his veiled face round the circle of pale spectators, Tremble also at each other. <break time="0.8s" /> When the friend shows his inmost heart to his friend, then deem me a monster for the symbol beneath which I have lived and die. <break time="0.8s" /> I look around me, and, lo, on every visage a Black Veil, he cried, and his hearers shrank from one another in mutual fear. <break time="0.8s" /> Father Hooper fell back upon his pillow, a veiled corpse with a faint smile on his lips, and they buried him with the veil still on his face. <break time="0.8s" /> The grass of many years has sprung up and withered on that grave, and good Father Hoopers face has long since mouldered beneath the Black Veil.
